pages.text:
Maitri Amin
EXTC B.Tech 2023, VJTI
Morgan Stanley (On- Campus)
FTE Technology Analyst Interview Experience
OVERVIEW
There were 4 rounds: Online test, Technical interview 1, Technical interview 2 and HR
interview . Students from circuit branches and MCA were allowed with CPI above 7.5 .
ROUND 1 - ONLINE TEST (1 hour 40 minutes)
Date: 28th July 2022 (Online)
There were 3 sections that had individual time limits, it could not be revisited.
1. Coding (60 Minutes): This was the first section which had 3 coding questions and
the questions were of medium difficulty level. For solving coding questions your
focus should be passing as many test cases as possible rather than writing an
optimized code. Most of the questions could be solved with a brute force
approach.
●
Question 1: A manufacturing firm has n outlets each with a unique ID ranging from
0 to n-1. Each outlet receives orders to supply items. Positive number denotes the
count of items present in the outlet and negative number denotes the count of out
of stock items. The task was to find a pair of outlets where one outlet can fulfill the
need of the other outlet. (Certain conditions were also given for making the pairs).
I was not able to clearly understand the question as it was given in a long story
format and was able to pass 9/12 test cases.
●
Question 2: A company has n employees with a unique ID for each employee
from 0 to n-1. Each employee has one manager and a manager does not have
more than two employees working under him. The manager and employee pair is
given. The task is to build a hierarchy between them and then do the boundary
order traversal.

In each pair the first element represents the employee and the second element
represents the manager. (The employee having manager as -1 is assumed to be
the head of the company and is the root node in the binary tree).
Input: n=7
6 -1, 5 6, 2 5, 0 2, 1 6, 3 1, 4 1
Output: 6 5 2 0 3 4 1
In this question my approach was to first make a binary tree and then do the
boundary order traversal. I managed to pass all the test cases (12/12).
●
Question 3: Given an array of n integers. Find the sum of the minimum between
the count of elements smaller than the element at the ith index on the left side
and the count of elements greater than the element at the ith index on the right
side.
Input: n=8
2  5  9  7  10  3  1  8
0       1         2        3        4        5       6         7
Output: 5
For index 0: Count of elements on left smaller than the 2: 0
Count of elements on right greater than the 2: 6
Minimum of both the counts: 0
For index 1:
Count of elements on left smaller than the 5: 1
Count of elements on right greater than the 5: 4
Minimum of both the counts: 1

For index 2:
Count of elements on left smaller than the 9: 2
Count of elements on right greater than the 9: 1
Minimum of both the counts: 1
Similarly find the minimum count for all the indices and add them.
I don't remember the exact approach but I was able to pass the test cases (12/12).
Note: For the coding questions you need to write the entire code including taking the
input and displaying the output.
2. Debugging (20 Minutes): This section had 7 debugging questions which were to
be solved in 20 minutes. Initially an option was given to choose the preferred
programming language (C++, Java, Python). Questions were based on Syntax
errors, Logical errors and completion of functions. Questions were of easy to
medium difficulty level. I was able to solve 4 to 5 questions.
3. Aptitude (20 Minutes): This section had 10 questions of easy to medium difficulty.
I was able to solve 7 to 8 questions. General aptitude questions were solved.
A total of 17 students (14 B.Tech + 3 MCA) were shortlisted for the interview.

ROUND 2 - TECHNICAL INTERVIEW (1 hour 10minutes)
Date: 1st August 2022 (Offline)
The interview was mostly based on Core CS Subjects and DSA. They asked questions
on OOPs concept and DSA.
1.
What is the difference between Encapsulation and Abstraction ?
2. What is the difference between static variables and instance variables ?
3. What is the difference between abstract classes and instances ?
4. What are virtual functions ?
5. An easy DSA question based on string.
Given a string str1 and another string str2. Check if str2 is the rotation of str1.
Initially I got confused but later on I was able to give the correct solution.
Link to the Question
6. The question was to construct a BST from an unsorted array but the size of the
array is not fixed. The elements are coming one after the other. (So the array is
dynamic).
Input: 6  7  4  5  9  8  2
Always understand the question and if you have any doubt ask the interviewer
about it before giving the solution. In my case I assumed that the size of the array
is fixed and all the elements are given beforehand and gave an approach where
the array needs to be sorted first. But the interviewer corrected me and told me
that all the elements are not given initially hence you cannot sort the array.
I was able to give the correct solution and wrote the code for the same.

7.
Given an array of integers and an input number. Find the count of a number
smaller than the input number and whose absolute difference with the input
number is minimum.
Input: 5 7 9 7 5 4 3 8 5 6 7
6
Output: 3
Input number is 6, elements smaller than 6 are 3, 4 and 5. The difference of 5 and
6 is the minimum so the answer is the count of 5 i.e. 3.
I gave a map based approach, the interviewer asked me to optimize it, but I was
not able to give an optimized approach. As we were running out of time, he
moved to the next question.
8. Discussion about one of my projects.
9. Why did I use MongoDB and what is the difference between SQL and NoSQL
databases?
For theory topics always give the definition first, then explain the concept in layman's
language and conclude it with an example.
9 students (8 B.Tech + 1 MCA) were selected for the Technical Interview 2.

ROUND 3 - TECHNICAL INTERVIEW (1 hour 15minutes)
Date: 1st August 2022 (Offline)
The interview was mostly based on Resume and System Design.
1.
Firstly the interviewer asked me how my day was so far and then asked me to
describe one of my projects. After I finished explaining the project he asked me
why I used mongoDB. What are the unique features in the project ? I used
Razorpay for an online payment feature so asked me how APIs work and how
would you implement a cancel payment feature.
We discussed the projects, unique features and how to add new features for
about 15-20 minutes. So be through with the projects that are mentioned in the
resume.
2. Then I was told to describe how my internship was and what my role was ?
3. One of the interviewers asked me about what I like about Mumbai. I said that
Mumbai has good connectivity and it's very easy to go from one place to another.
Based on this he asked me to design an algorithm which helps the BUS system for
their efficient working. I knew this was a system design question so I said that I
don't know system design. The interviewers were very kind and told me not to
worry as they won't ask me to write the code. We had a discussion on this. The
interviewers helped me come up with an algorithm. Firstly they told me to think of
the factors/attributes that are important for designing the algorithm. I gave about
10 - 12 factors like names of the bus-stations, distance between the bus-stations,
ticket price, route that a particular bus takes, no. of tickets sold etc. Then I said,
our next task is to store the data and find a relationship between them. I said that
different data structures can be used to store the data. The bus-station name and
distance between them can be visualized as a graph and a weighted graph data
structure can be used to store that data. Next, a linked list can be used to store
the route that is taken by the bus. And for the remaining data a simple map and
vector can be used. I said one of the approaches to increase the efficiency of the
BUS system could be to analyze the tickets sold based on time and accordingly
increase/decrease the frequency of the bus. I also suggested 2 or 3 more
approaches. The interviewers were satisfied with my approach. We had a
discussion for 25-30 minutes.

4. Based on the previous question the interviewer drew a picture on the paper
where it has a bus and passengers entered the bus from the back gate and exited
from the front gate. He told me to identify the data structure and it was very easy
and I gave the answer very quickly. I was a queue data structure.
5. I was asked one sorting question (Don’t exactly remember the question). Also
asked about different sorting algorithms and the time complexity.
6. I was asked a simple puzzle which I already knew.
Link to the puzzle
7.
It was a situation question where I wanted to start a new Cake shop. What are the
factors that need to be considered before opening a new Cake shop ? I gave 2 to
3 factors that are important and the interviewer was satisfied with my answer.
All the candidates who were selected for Technical Interview 2 were told to give the HR
interview.

ROUND 4 - HR INTERVIEW (15minutes)
Date: 1st August 2022 (Offline)
The interview was mostly based on Resume Projects and General HR questions.
1.
Describe your academic journey till now. And how did you prepare for JEE and
other competitive exams?
2. Small discussion on some of my projects. And also how can I increase security for
one of my projects ?
3. While working in a team how will you coordinate with the other team-mates and
what will you do if one of your team members doesn’t work properly ?
4. What did you learn from your internship ?
Finally, results were announced and 4 students (all B.Tech) were offered the FTE offers. I
am very grateful to be one of them.

TIPS
1.
Never lie on your resume and be thorough with the projects and internships
mentioned in the resume.
2. If you don't understand the question ask the interviewer and clarify it before giving
the solution/answer.
3. Have a look at the interview experiences and analyze the type of questions asked
by a particular company and prepare accordingly.
4. Practice 3 to 4 DSA questions regularly and keep on revising the core CS subjects
which will help you better understand the concept.
5. While learning Core CS subjects make proper notes so that it can be helpful for
revision.
6. One day before the interview, revise CS subjects, practice standard DSA
questions ( 1 or 2 ) from each topic and have a look at your projects as well.
7.
Always ask one or two questions at the end of each interview round.
